rules.why: Evaluating dynamic string input as code can lead to arbitrary code execution.
rules.fix: Avoid eval(), new Function(), or exec() on dynamic input. Use safe data parsing or static dispatch.

rules.why: Passing interpolated strings into a shell command allows shell command injection.
rules.fix: Use execFile or subprocess with an explicit array of argument strings instead of shell execution.

rules.why: Constructing SQL queries via string concatenation or interpolation enables SQL injection.
rules.fix: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements with parameter placeholders.

rules.why: Joining file system paths with unvalidated user input creates path traversal risk.
rules.fix: Sanitize path inputs or verify path containment using path.resolve() / path.relative() check.

rules.why: Constructing outbound HTTP requests from non-literal URL inputs creates Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) risk.
rules.fix: Validate URL schemes and hostname allowlists before initiating outbound requests.

rules.why: Deserializing untrusted data with pickle.loads, yaml.load, or node vm execution allows code execution.
rules.fix: Use yaml.safe_load, json.loads, or structured data formats instead of executable object deserialization.

rules.why: An asynchronous Promise call is neither awaited, returned, nor caught, causing unhandled promise rejections.
rules.fix: Await the promise, return it, or attach a .catch() handler.

rules.why: Catching an exception without logging, handling, or rethrowing hides unexpected system failures.
rules.fix: Log the error, handle the failure condition explicitly, or rethrow.

rules.why: Catching bare except or except Exception catches system signals and unrecoverable errors indiscriminately.
rules.fix: Catch specific exception classes or re-raise after logging.

rules.why: Using mutable default arguments (e.g., def f(x=[])) retains state across function invocations.
rules.fix: Use None as the default argument value and initialize the mutable object inside the function body.

rules.why: Network request initiated without explicit timeout configuration can hang indefinitely.
rules.fix: Pass a timeout option or set signal / AbortController timeout on HTTP client calls.

rules.why: Awaiting asynchronous operations inside a loop runs operations sequentially when parallel execution may be possible.
rules.fix: Use Promise.all() or asyncio.gather() if loop iterations have no ordering dependencies.

rules.why: Using MD5 or SHA1 in authentication, password, or security token contexts is cryptographically broken.
rules.fix: Use bcrypt, argon2, scrypt, or SHA-256/SHA-512 for cryptographic integrity.

rules.why: Math.random() or random.random() is not cryptographically secure for generating keys, nonces, or tokens.
rules.fix: Use crypto.getRandomValues(), crypto.randomBytes(), or secrets module in Python.

rules.why: Literal string matches a known API key or credential pattern.
rules.fix: Store credentials in environment variables. For deep secret scanning, route to EVIDIQ Redact.

rules.why: Configuring Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * alongside credentialed requests allows unauthorized cross-site data access.
rules.fix: Specify trusted origin domains explicitly instead of wildcard '*'.

rules.why: Debugger statements or debug logging of potential secret identifiers remain in production code.
rules.fix: Remove debugger statements and console.log / print of sensitive data before committing.

rules.why: Cyclomatic complexity of a function exceeds the configured threshold.
rules.fix: Refactor complex conditional branches into smaller helper functions.

rules.why: Deeply nested control structures degrade readability and maintainability.
rules.fix: Use guard clauses and early returns to flatten nested blocks.

rules.why: Function length exceeds the maximum recommended line count.
rules.fix: Split long functions into cohesive single-responsibility functions.

rules.why: Parameter count exceeds threshold.
rules.fix: Group related parameters into an options object or parameter data structure.

rules.why: Identical code block detected multiple times.
rules.fix: Extract duplicate logic into a shared helper function.
